title: R’ Shila of Dinavah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Shabbat, chapter 2, at the supplied דה״ה [a matching passage is Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:5], where the sages of Caesarea speak in Rabbi Shila of Dinavah’s name.
Perhaps, Hyman says, the passage in Makkot 2:6, “the sages of Caesarea in the name of R’ Shilah,” SHOULD READ R’ Shila of Dinavah.

In the passage Hyman cites from Ruth Rabbah, R’ Shila of Dinavah says, “The needy man—אהן מסכינא הב הינק מיניה” [the Aramaic wording remains uncertain]. (Hyman explains: What the poor man asks you for, he asks from his own share, for you have taken his share.)
Vayikra Rabbah 34:9 cites the saying, with the name R’ Shilah of Denuha.

notes.text: The supplied Bereshit Rabbah locator says 5:19 and the Shabbat locator has the irregular prefix דה״ה. Vayikra Rabbah 34:9 contains the poor-man saying with Shilah of Denuha. The supplied locators remain source questions.

The saved whole Venice Shabbat2:5 scalar has רבנן דקיסרין בשם רבי שילא דינוה, supporting that occurrence’s full Rabbi and the reported relation. It does not explain supplied דה״ה. The earlier Vayikra34:9 comparison is inherited, not newly inspected; the Bereshit5:19 location remains unlocated rather than proved nonexistent. The Aramaic poor-man saying is retained explicitly beside Hyman’s own share explanation, without guessing הינק more confidently. Shila/Shilah and Dinavah/Denuha remain distinct. His PERHAPS IT SHOULD READ proposal in Makkot retains both hedge and emendation force; no full title is borrowed for uninspected occurrences.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, pp. 1113–1114) has וברו״ר פ״ה־יט, which points to Ruth Rabbah, where section 5:9 comments on Ruth 2:19 and gives the shorter “your wealth is in him.” The supplied transcription instead names Bereshit Rabbah. Vayikra Rabbah 34:9 has a fuller parallel with הונך, “your wealth,” alongside Hyman’s הינק. Both the Venice and Guggenheimer texts of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:5 name Shila of Dinavah in the Caesarean sages’ attribution. The consulted Makkot 2:6 names Shilah without the place-name, which Hyman tentatively supplies.
